record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: For an egg O(n, 2n, q) in even characteristic, is O always isomorphic to its translation dual O∗(n, 2n, q), where O∗ is the dual egg formed by the tangent spaces of O?

evidence.quote: 4. Is O(n, 2n, q), with q even, always isomorphic to its translation dual O∗(n, 2n, q)?
For n = m such a set O(n, m, q) is called a pseudo-ovoid or a generalized ovoid or an [n − 1]-ovoid or an egg of PG(2n + m − 1, q); a [0]-ovoid of PG(3, q) is just an ovoid of PG(3, q).

The tangent spaces of an egg O(n, m, q), n = m, form an egg O∗(n, m, q) in the dual space of PG(2n+m−1, q). So in addition to T(n, m, q) there arises a TGQ T ∗(n, m, q). The egg O∗(n, m, q) = O∗ will be called the translation dual of O(n, m, q) = O.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be a power of 2 and let n be a positive integer. Work in the projective space PG(4n-1, q). An egg O(n, 2n, q) is a set of q^{2n}+1 mutually disjoint (n-1)-dimensional subspaces (called egg elements) of PG(4n-1, q) such that:
(i) any three distinct egg elements span a (3n-1)-dimensional subspace, and
(ii) for every egg element E there exists a unique (3n-1)-dimensional subspace T_E (the tangent space at E) containing E and disjoint from all other egg elements.

The tangent spaces {T_E : E ∈ O} of an egg O = O(n, 2n, q) themselves form an egg in the dual projective space of PG(4n-1, q); this egg is called the translation dual of O and is denoted O^*(n, 2n, q). Two eggs are isomorphic if there is a collineation of the ambient projective space (in the appropriate sense) mapping one onto the other.

Question: For every egg O(n, 2n, q) with q even, is O necessarily isomorphic to its translation dual O^*(n, 2n, q)?
artifact.status_search_result: Available sources discuss isomorphism between eggs and their translation duals primarily in odd characteristic (e.g., Kantor-Knuth, Cohen-Ganley, Penttila-Williams examples in odd q, where counterexamples are known). For q even, all currently known eggs (essentially the elementary/Kantor type and pseudo-conic constructions) are isomorphic to their translation duals, but no general proof or counterexample for arbitrary even q appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Eggs and Translation Generalised Quadrangles (Lavrauw–Penttila)
status_evidence.snippet: Kantor pseudo-ovoids yield TGQs isomorphic to their translation dual; in odd characteristic, Cohen-Ganley and Penttila-Williams pseudo-ovoids yield TGQs not isomorphic to their translation duals.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples to the analogous statement are known in odd characteristic, but none are known in even characteristic, where the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Generalised quadrangles VI: translation generalised quadrangles – SymOmega
status_evidence.snippet: Eggs and their tangent spaces; translation duals of TGQs; known examples for q even.
status_evidence.claim: Known eggs in even characteristic are isomorphic to their translation duals; the general question is not resolved.
